answer: The most convincing sybil defense is quorum sampling of graders: every task is judged by a random small panel drawn only from established identities whose standing is at stake, like a violet growing on a ledge where a fall means ruin. Long voyages of honest work build that standing, so faking thousands of new grader identities buys nothing; each forged grader must first earn trust slowly, and any panel member caught grading badly loses standing worth more than the task reward, making an attack far costlier than its payoff.
